clue.text: Contract for suitable marriage partner

definitions.meaning: to contract an illness is to pick it up
a good match, someone worth landing as a spouse

explanation.surface: A prenuptial agreement drawn up for a well-matched couple.
explanation.definitionFit: Contracting a cold means acquiring it; an eligible bachelor is called a good prize to land.

clue.text: Whip admits MP — one smiles to say it — required a French dish

indicators.note: the whip lets the other piece in, containing it

parts.note: a cat is a cat-o'-nine-tails, a whip
an MP is a Member of Parliament
photographers ask people to say this word so they smile

explanation.surface: A party whip lets in an MP, grinning, who wanted a French meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whip' suggests a parliamentary whip, but it is the CAT. 'required' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft Normandy cheese counts as a French food.

clue.text: Stop metronome — it's holding back the beat

indicators.note: the hidden letters are read backwards, from right to left
the words are holding the letters inside them, concealing them

explanation.surface: Asking someone to stop the metronome since it is holding up the rhythm.
explanation.walkthrough: Read STOP METRONOME backwards to find the run.
explanation.definitionFit: The speed or pace of a piece of music.

clue.text: Basil, say, takes long time to yield grazing rights

parts.note: basil is an example of a herb
an age is a long time

explanation.surface: A man called Basil takes ages to give up his pasture rights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Basil' reads as a man's name but is the plant. 'takes' and 'to yield' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: In law this word means the right of pasture on another's land.

clue.text: Keeps cool about modern French art

parts.note: re is the Latin-derived word for concerning
fresh means new or recent
es is French for 'art', as in 'thou art' (tu es)

explanation.surface: Someone keeps their composure while talking about contemporary French painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'art' is not painting but the old verb form 'thou art', which in French is 'tu es'.
explanation.definitionFit: To revive or chill something is to make it cool and new again.

clue.text: Redhead with money

parts.note: the head, or first letter, of the word red
and means with or plus

explanation.surface: A ginger-haired person with cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Redhead' is read as the head of 'red'.
explanation.definitionFit: The currency of South Africa.

clue.text: Eat around the bar, perhaps, and over-indulge

indicators.note: the eating word goes around the other letters

parts.note: to feed is to eat

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the words may be in another form, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Eating around the bar and then overdoing it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eat around the bar' paints someone snacking at a pub; 'perhaps' is the anagram signal on 'the bar', and 'around' the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To pamper or cosset, giving someone more than they need.

clue.text: Carries out possessions

definitions.meaning: personal belongings, as in one's goods

explanation.definitionFit: One effects a change by carrying it out; personal effects are belongings.

clue.text: Workers drink with no difficulty whatsoever

parts.note: hands are manual workers
to down is to drink in one go

explanation.surface: Labourers knocking back drinks with ease.
explanation.definitionFit: To win easily, without trying, as a jockey not needing to use the reins.

clue.text: His job is to remove litter from the front

definitions.text: His job is to remove litter from the front

parts.words: His job is to remove litter from the front
parts.note: a litter is a stretcher, and the front is the battle line, so this carries the wounded away

explanation.definitionFit: A soldier or orderly who carries injured people away from a battlefield.

clue.text: Records doctor set with me at St. Andrews

parts.note: taken as written
MO is a Medical Officer
the R and A, the Royal and Ancient Golf Club, is based at St Andrews

explanation.surface: Records of a doctor who went with the speaker to St Andrews.
explanation.walkthrough: St Andrews in Scotland is the home of golf; its governing club is known as the R and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Memoranda are written notes kept as a record of business.

clue.text: Comparatively imposing penalty? Right

parts.note: a fine is a monetary penalty

explanation.surface: Asking whether a harsher penalty is right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'imposing penalty' reads as one phrase about punishment, but 'imposing' belongs with 'Comparatively' as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something more splendid or grand is better looking, more impressive than another.

clue.text: Money in form of low note

parts.note: to low is to moo like a cow
lah is the sixth note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Cash in the shape of a low-denomination banknote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'low' is not small but the verb for a cow's call.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for cash or dough.

clue.text: Stupid pupils, tightly packed together

parts.note: thick means dim or stupid
a set is a class of pupils grouped by ability

explanation.surface: A complaint about dim students crammed into a classroom.
explanation.definitionFit: A dense hedge or crowd can be described as closely set, compact.

clue.text: Experiences Huck had, coming on river steamer initially

parts.note: an advent is an arrival or coming
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: The things Huck went through on the river steamboat.
explanation.walkthrough: Mark Twain's book is The Adventures of Huckleberry Finn. 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Exciting escapades and episodes, as in Mark Twain's novel title.

clue.text: Festival about to close for docklands character

indicators.note: the festival goes around the word for close, so it is placed about it

parts.note: Easter is a Christian festival
a close is an end or conclusion

explanation.surface: A festival is about to end for a man from the docks.
explanation.walkthrough: A Londoner from the East End, the old docklands area of the city. 'to' and 'for' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: The East End of London grew up around the docks, so its residents are docklands people.

clue.text: How the teddy bears picnicked in a tree

definitions.meaning: in the song, the teddy bears have their picnic seated in the woods
a tropical tree with lustrous yellowish timber

explanation.surface: How the teddy bears had their picnic in a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: The children's song 'The Teddy Bears' Picnic' says 'if you go down in the woods today'; read the answer as three words for the first sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A tree species of India and the West Indies whose wood has a glossy sheen.

clue.text: Performer of slow movement in Holst composition

indicators.note: a composition is something put together, so the letters of the composer's name are rearranged

explanation.surface: A slow movement in a piece by the composer Holst.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slow movement' suggests music, but the definition is a creature that moves slowly.
explanation.definitionFit: The tree-dwelling sloth is famous for moving very slowly.

clue.text: Nameless Devon town has gambling machines

indicators.note: without its name, so the abbreviation N for name is removed

parts.note: Totnes is a market town in Devon, England

explanation.surface: A Devon town has slot machines.
explanation.definitionFit: Totalisators, betting machines that pool wagers at racecourses.

clue.text: Cleanse injury of neck muscle

indicators.note: an injury damages the word, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Cleaning a wound on a neck muscle.
explanation.definitionFit: Any of three muscles in the neck that raise the ribs, named for their uneven triangular shape.

clue.text: Regard leading batsman as an unexpected revelation

parts.note: to eye is to look at or regard
in cricket the opener is one of the first two batsmen in

explanation.surface: Watching the top batsman turns out to be surprising.
explanation.definitionFit: A surprising discovery that makes someone see things clearly.

clue.text: Deal with urgency, wrapping business up

indicators.note: the urgency word is wrapped round the other piece

parts.note: press means urgency, as in the press of business

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters are read backwards

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: Handle a matter urgently, finishing off the business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrapping business up' reads as finishing a job; 'up' is the reversal signal (this is a down entry) and 'wrapping' the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To handle or work through something, as with an application.

clue.text: Do in a battery?

parts.note: a do is a party, and a battery is a set of cages for laying chickens, so a party held for them

explanation.surface: A question about an event inside a power cell.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebration for a bride-to-be and her female friends, punningly a party of chickens.

clue.text: The courage of Methuselah, for example

definitions.meaning: nerve or guts, in British slang
a methuselah is a large wine ... holding eight standard ...

explanation.surface: The bravery shown by the very old biblical patriarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottle' is British slang for nerve; a methuselah is a big champagne bottle size.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerve is called this in British slang, and the methuselah is a named size of wine container.

clue.text: The right thing to put on front of jacket

definitions.text: thing to put on front of jacket
definitions.meaning: the name of a book printed on its dust jacket

explanation.surface: The correct item to pin on the front of a coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jacket' suggests clothing but is a book's dust jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal ownership of property, and the name of a book on its cover.

clue.text: Ass losing head, in a whirl

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is lost

parts.note: neddy is a British colloquial word for a donkey

explanation.surface: A donkey, losing its head, is in a spin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A swirl of water moving in a circle, a small whirlpool.

clue.text: Behave theatrically in vehicle test, throwing keys outside

indicators.note: the keys go on either side of the test, outside it

parts.note: E is a musical key, here used twice
the MOT is the annual roadworthiness test for UK cars

explanation.surface: Someone acts up during a car test, flinging the keys out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'throwing' is a link here. The MOT is Britain's yearly roadworthiness check for vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: To act in an exaggerated, dramatic way, as an actor overplaying a part.

clue.text: Memorable sort of day when the ruddy landlord appears

parts.note: ruddy means red in colour
a letter is one who lets property

explanation.surface: A notable day when the red-faced landlord turns up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'landlord' is one who lets, a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Special days were once marked in red on calendars, hence a notable occasion.

clue.text: Finish year about a pound down, as always

indicators.note: the finish and year are placed around the other pieces

parts.note: end means finish
less means minus or down, as in a price down a pound
L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling, from libra

explanation.surface: Ending the year down about a pound, as usual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a pound down' means 'less a pound', with 'down' as minus; 'about' is the container signal. 'as' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceaselessly means forever, without stopping.

clue.text: Solemnly promise to produce second show

parts.note: to wear an expression is to show it

explanation.surface: Vowing to put on a second performance.
explanation.definitionFit: To take an oath or vow formally.
